sources.entry: colour-science - Implementing a comprehensive number of colour theory transformations and algorithms.

summary.one_liner: Colour is a BSD-3-Clause Python package providing algorithms and datasets for colour science, including colour space conversions, colour appearance models, colour difference metrics, and spectral computations.
summary.what_it_does: The README documents a Python package imported as `colour` that covers colour science. It includes a conversion graph (colour.convert) that routes between spectral distributions, XYZ and RGB spaces, with verbose path display. It offers chromatic adaptation methods (CIE 1994, CMCCAT2000, Von Kries, and others), colour appearance models (CIECAM02, CAM16, Hellwig2022, Kim2009, sCAM, ZCAM), and colour difference formulas such as CIE 1976, CIE 2000, CAM16-UCS and DIN99. Further sections cover colorimetry (spectral to XYZ, illuminants, CMFs), colour rendering and quality indices (CRI, CQS, TM-30-18), spectral recovery from XYZ or RGB, CCT computation, RGB colourspace definitions and transfer functions, and image and LUT I/O. Plotting helpers and optical phenomena such as sky luminance models and thin-film interference are also included.
use_cases: convert colour values between colour spaces
compute colour difference (delta E) between two colours
calculate colour rendering index or colour quality of a light source
estimate correlated colour temperature from chromaticity
read LUT and image files for colour pipeline work
colour blindness simulation of spectral data
notable: Very broad coverage: dozens of colour spaces, transfer functions, and appearance models in one package
colour.convert shows the conversion path between representations
Includes spectral data sets such as colour checker and standard illuminants
caveats: The README excerpt does not state platform limits or Python version requirements
Some features (e.g. plotting) are shown with examples but their dependencies are not detailed in the excerpt
